main_text.l: Æschylum quidam ait: Ἀλλοῖα μορφὴν λαμ-πάδας τε πυρφόρους μόρον.[?]
7. Quia ut ἐπιχαιρέκακοι in medijs successibus τεταγμένοι[?]: sic ἐπιχαιρέκακοι in ipsis tentationum paroxysmis τεταμμένοι[?] sunt.
8. Quia Dei iudicio in his omnibus stadium est. Sunt autem pij, cùm tentationis igne explorantur, congratulatione: impij autem, cùm ἐπιχαιρεκακίᾳ[?] hilarescunt, gemitu profequendi.

l.i: Propterea sacrificabit sagenæ suæ, & suffiet reti suo: quia per illa impinguata est portio eius, et cibus eius pingue(pecus.)

main_text.l: Phrases [illegible, ~10 letters], Sacrificare sagenæ: &, Suffimentum reti adolere, idem plane significat: videlicet, fortitudini suæ bellicæ, industriæ, potentiæ, prudentiæ, acceptas ferre victorias & successus: non Deo. Eius persuasionis exemplum in Rabsacis oratione exstat, Isa.36.
7. ARGVMENTVM HABACVCI, à sacrilega Chaldæorum persuasione de suis viribus.
Indigni sunt victoria, qui eam nō Deo, sed sibi ipsis adscribunt. Non enim nobis,

page.notes: The Greek in the first paragraph and in verses 7 and 8 is hard to read from the scan and may be wrong letter by letter; those words carry [?]. The Greek word after "Phrases" is not legible and is given as illegible. The margin note beside verse XVI is in a small type and "Lectio" is partly unclear; it is copied as best read. Long s is plain s throughout; u/v and i/j are normalised. The printed spellings "suffiet", "Suffimentum" and "successus" are kept as printed. The bottom "1" is taken as a gathering signature.
